note: Global Peers: the US and global names that lead, supply or mirror Indian stocks. Edit by hand and run python tools/build_peers.py. `rel` is the relationship (peer = same business listed abroad, customer = buys from the Indian company, supplier = sells to it, parent = majority owner, bellwether = reports first and sets the tone). `for` limits a global name to some Indian codes in the group; leave it out to pair it with all of them. `lag` is set by the tool from the exchange: Asian closes come before India's (same day), US and European closes come after (next India session).

groups.name: Optical fibre & AI data-centre connectivity
groups.why: HFCL and Sterlite Tech sell optical fibre, cable and connectivity into the same data-centre build-out that Corning serves; Lumentum and Coherent are the optical-components end of it.

india.note: telecom gear rather than fibre; added for the same AI-network read-across

global.name: Corning
global.note: optical fibre and connectivity for AI data centres - the closest listed replica of the fibre business

global.name: Lumentum
global.note: optical transceivers and lasers for AI data centres

groups.name: Memory & chips
groups.why: GNG Electronics refurbishes and sells computing hardware whose cost and demand follow the memory cycle that Samsung, SK hynix and Micron report on.

global.name: SK hynix
global.note: memory (DRAM, HBM) - closes before India's market, so the read-across is same-day

global.name: Micron
global.note: US memory maker - reports quarterly guidance the whole memory chain trades on

groups.name: AI cloud & GPU servers
groups.why: Netweb builds GPU servers (as Super Micro does) and E2E Networks rents GPU capacity (as Nebius and CoreWeave do); NVIDIA supplies all of them and its results set the tone.

global.name: NVIDIA
global.note: GPUs for every name in this group; its quarter sets the whole chain's tone

global.name: Nebius
global.note: GPU cloud - the listed replica of E2E Networks

global.name: Super Micro Computer
global.note: AI server maker - the listed replica of Netweb

groups.name: Bloom Energy supply chain
groups.why: MTAR Technologies makes hot boxes and other assemblies for Bloom Energy's fuel cells; Bloom is its largest customer, so Bloom's orders and results lead MTAR's.

groups.name: Power equipment parents

global.name: GE Vernova

groups.name: IT services vs Accenture

global.name: Accenture

global.name: Cognizant
global.note: US-listed peer with an India delivery base
